thread:
acme-app: Hey team — our monthly credits just dropped to 0 during a bulk embed job even though midnight reset should have been in ~30m. We retried failed requests a bunch (client retries). Any chance retries are double-counting or not covered by refill?

Maria (Support): Sorry to hear that — can you share org id + approx timestamps of the run? Also paste a short repro (curl or SDK snippet) if available.

acme-app: Org: org_9XcPl. Started bulk job @ 2026-03-15T22:40:00Z, massive retry storm from 22:43–22:55. Visible UI showed ~4000 tokens left at 22:42, then 0 at 22:50. We were expecting reset at 23:00 UTC.

Alejandra (AcctMgr): Putting a hold on billing escalations. We'll review whether auto-credit applies. Do you have request IDs for a couple failed requests?

acme-app: pasted a few request ids in DM. Quick repro snippet we used (Python):

```python
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embed-xxl", input=batch)
# naive retry: for _ in range(5): try: resp = client... except: sleep(1); continue
```

Maria (Support): Thanks. Two things: 1) retries are charged per request (each attempt consumes tokens). 2) our monthly refill runs near the top of the hour but UI cache TTL can delay visible balance by seconds–minutes.

Sam (Eng): Adding more detail from runtime: retries that don't include idempotency keys are indistinguishable from new requests and will be billed again. Also during a heavy retry storm the edge rate limiter can return 429s which cause more retries -> amplification.

Jonah (SRE): Related note: we observed a small window where the refill calculation used stale edge-cache entries for org quotas when there was a high write rate to the quota DB. That could postpone the visible refill and allow clients to think they're still in the previous window and keep retrying. We have a fix rolling to tighten cache TTLs.

acme-app: So to confirm — our retries definitely consumed tokens and the refill arrived a little late due to cache TTL? That explains the customer surprise.

Maria (Support): Correct. We reproduced similar behaviour in sandbox with a tight retry loop + no idempotency header. We recommended: implement exponential backoff + jitter, and include an idempotency key for bulk jobs when possible.

Sam (Eng): Also, you can use the per-request rate-limit headers: Example: `Retry-After: 3` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining` in responses — respect them to avoid amplification. If you do a bulk job, prefer batching fewer items per request and fewer parallel workers so you don't hit burst/window limits.

acme-app: Any temporary mitigation you can do from our side or you can credit tokens? This was a production customer run.

Alejandra (AcctMgr): We're issuing a one-time goodwill credit while we investigate (ticket #SUP-2026-1143). We'll apply it and follow up in the support ticket.

billing-bot: Credit applied: +50k tokens to org_9XcPl, reference SUP-2026-1143.

Maria (Support): For long term: if you expect big bulk uploads, schedule them after the monthly refill, or request a Dedicated pool to avoid monthly-bucket exhaustion. We can also whitelist large batches during onboarding migrations on a case-by-case basis.

acme-app: Appreciate it. We'll add idempotency keys, exponential backoff, and throttle parallelism. Also will move large migrations to dedicated windows.

Sam (Eng): Filed follow-up engineering ticket to add a best-practices guide for bulk embeddings and sample client retry code (ENG-PR-789). Will ping when live.

Jonah (SRE): Fix for cache TTLs is in canary. We expect improved visible refill within the next deploy (ETA 12–24h).

acme-app: Thanks all :heart: — closing thread once credit shows and we test the client changes.

Maria (Support): I'll mark the support ticket as in-progress and update once credit is visible. Reopen here if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
